Calculate the height of a tree based on its diameter at breast height and an allometry parameter

Source: R/Processes.R
height.Rd

Calculate the height of a tree based on its diameter at breast height and an allometry parameter

Usage

height(dbh, parHeight)

Arguments

dbh

A numeric value representing the diameter at breast height of the tree in cm.

parHeight

A numeric value representing the species height allometry.

Value

A numeric vector (or torch.Tensor, for tensor input) with the height of the tree in m.

Details

This function calculates the height of a tree based on the diameter at breast height (dbh) and a parameter parHeight.

The height is calculated using the formula: $$height = \left( \exp \left( \frac{(\text{dbh} \times \text{parHeight})}{(\text{dbh} + 100)} \right) - 1 \right) \times 100 + 0.001$$ where dbh is the diameter at breast height of the tree in cm and parHeight is an allometric species specific parameter.

As the diameter grows, the height approaches \((\exp(\text{parHeight}) - 1) \times 100\) m: 35 m for parHeight = 0.3, 65 m for 0.5, 101 m for 0.7. When the height parameter is fitted (the first column of the competition parameters), FINN keeps it between 0.3 and \(\log(2.3) \approx 0.83\), so no species can grow taller than 130 m, the physical limit of tree height (Koch et al. 2004). Values below 0.3 suit small trees and shrubs; set createProcess(lower = ) for them.

References

Koch, G. W., Sillett, S. C., Jennings, G. M. & Davis, S. D. (2004). The limits to tree height. Nature 428, 851-854.

See also

competition(), which ranks the cohorts of a patch by this height

Examples

# a 30-cm tree of a species with parHeight = 0.5 is about 12 m tall
height(30, 0.5)
#> [1] 12.2315
# the same diameter for a tall-growing and a short-growing species
height(c(30), c(0.5,0.3))
#> [1] 12.231501  7.169349
# two diameters of one species
height(c(30,20), c(0.5))
#> [1] 12.231501  8.691405

# the height curve of three species; the asymptote is (exp(parHeight) - 1) * 100 m
dbh <- seq(0, 150, by = 10)
round(sapply(c(low = 0.3, mid = 0.5, tall = 0.7), function(p) height(dbh, p)), 1)
#>        low  mid tall
#>  [1,]  0.0  0.0  0.0
#>  [2,]  2.8  4.7  6.6
#>  [3,]  5.1  8.7 12.4
#>  [4,]  7.2 12.2 17.5
#>  [5,]  9.0 15.4 22.1
#>  [6,] 10.5 18.1 26.3
#>  [7,] 11.9 20.6 30.0
#>  [8,] 13.1 22.9 33.4
#>  [9,] 14.3 24.9 36.5
#> [10,] 15.3 26.7 39.3
#> [11,] 16.2 28.4 41.9
#> [12,] 17.0 29.9 44.3
#> [13,] 17.8 31.4 46.5
#> [14,] 18.5 32.7 48.5
#> [15,] 19.1 33.9 50.4
#> [16,] 19.7 35.0 52.2
